mechanism: Garlic has mild antiplatelet and anticoagulant properties that may theoretically potentiate the anticoagulant effects if folic acid is used in thrombotic conditions, though folic acid itself is not anticoagulant.
action: Monitor for unusual bleeding if high-dose garlic supplements are used concurrently with folic acid in patients on anticoagulant therapy; routine folic acid supplementation with dietary garlic poses minimal clinical concern.
